 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 30.12.2017 at about 10.30 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing No.KA-04- HY-3596, when they reached near T.Begur cross,
Tumkur- Bengaluru NH-4 road, at that time Tata 407 bearing No.KA-04-D- 5637 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the motor cycle.

As a result of the forced impact,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Government hospital, Nelamangala, after first aid treatment she was shifted to Victoria hospital, wherein he took the treatment as inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 55 years, working as a Carpenter and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata 407 vehicle bearing registration No.KA- 04-D-5637.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and filed their written statement.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of Tata 407 Vehicle bearing No.KA-04-D-5637 and its liability will be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provision u/s 134(c)
and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-HY-3596.
Further contended that the owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA-04-D-5637 was not possessing valid permit at the time of accident.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and highly exorbitant Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.

Contending the above facts,

6. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further denied the entire petition averments in toto.
Further contended that the vehicle involved in the accident has been duly insured with the respondent No.1 and it is valid from 25.2.2017 to 24.2.2018.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, inflated, huge and excessive.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA at about 10.30 a.m. near Thyamagondlu cross on Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-4 road, T.Begur, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

8. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.18 to Ex.P20.
9. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondents have not examined any witness on their behalf.
10. Heard the arguments.

11. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 12. ISSUE NO.1:-
During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents have denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition.
14. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
15. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of his evidence, he has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P5 such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
16.
On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by the petitioner on 1.1.2018.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Nelamangala Traffic Police in Cr.No.003/2018 against the driver of the Tata 407 bearing registration No.KA-04-D-5637 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar drawn by the I.O. also reveals the scene of incident, Ex.P3 is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to both vehicles and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of both the vehicles.
Ex.P4 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P5 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the Tata 407 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
17.

The counsel for the respondents have argued that the accident occurred due to the negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-HY-3596 and not on the part of the driver of the Tata 407 bearing No.KA-04-D-5637.
To substantiate the said facts, they have not examined any witness nor produced any documents to show that the accident occurred due to the negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle.
Further more, they have not challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the Tata 407.
On the other hand, the petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

18. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 19. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata 407 bearing No.KA-04-D-5637.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that he met with an accident on 30.12.2017 at about 10.30 a.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Government hospital,
then to Victoria hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact,
petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P4, which discloses the following injuries:

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 30.12.2017 to 10.1.2018 and underwent ORIF ILN tibia.

22. PW2 being the Orthopaedic surgeon has stated that the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg, fracture clavicle left, fracture ribs 2, 3 and 4th left and underwent internal fixation of tibia and other fractures treated conservatively.

23. Considering the oral evidence of PW1 & PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.

24. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 55 years, carpenter at Shilpa Wood Works, Bengaluru and getting an income of Rs.30,000/- per month i.e., Rs.1,000/- per day.
He has produced salary certificate marked at Ex.P7, which discloses that the petitioner was working as a skilled carpenter and was drawing a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day consolidated.
But the petitioner has not examined his employer or produced any acquaintance roll or bank pass book to show that he was getting Rs.1,000/- per day.
In the absence of such documents pertains to his avocation and income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner.

So,
considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner, if notional income of Rs.8,500/-
per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 30.12.2017 to 10.1.2018.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries; he might have taken rest and treatment at least for three months.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.25,500/- to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
25. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount of Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses.
On record he has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.12,363/-.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.12,363/- towards medical expenses.

26. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 55 years, skilled carpenter at Shilpa Wood Works, Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- per month i.e., Rs.1,000/- per day.
Due to the accident, he is not able to do his carpentry work and has become a layman.
He has produced x-ray at Ex.P11.

sentences.text: To prove the age, the petitioner has produced Aadhar card and ration card, which are marked at Ex.P8 & Ex.P9.
On perusal of the Aadhar card, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 2.3.1963.
The accident occurred on 30.12.2017, so as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 54 years.
So, same is considered as the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident.

28. PW2-Dr. Ramesh B has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained fracture both bones of left leg, fracture clavicle left and fracture ribs 2, 3 and 4th left and recently on 3.8.2019 he has examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of left lower limb is 26%, 13% of left upper limbs, 18% of whole body.
He has produced out patient card, case sheet and x- rays, which are marked at Ex.P18 to Ex.P20.
On perusal of cross- examination of PW2, fractures are united.

So,
considering the evidence of PW2 and his cross-examination, age, avocation of the petitioner and relative disability, if 15% of the disability is considered as whole body of disability of the petitioner, it will meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner age is already considered as 55 years the multiplier applicable to this age is 11.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,68,300/- under the head of loss of future earning.
30. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
So his happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out his life.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head of amenities.
31. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident he took the treatment as inpatient.
He has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 30.12.2017 to 10.1.2018.
So, one must attend him during the above said period.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.
32. PW2 doctor has stated in his evidence that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost of Rs.20,000/-.
Relying on the opinion of the doctor it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- for future medical expenses.

33. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
 Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000-00 2.
Loss of income during laid period Rs. 25,500-00 and rest period 3.

LIABILITY: On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata 407 bearing No.KA-04-D-5637.
35.
The respondent No.1 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-04-D-5637 and its validity.

The petitioner has produced copy of RC of the vehicle bearing No.KA-04-D-5637, insurance policy, permit, driving license, tax receipt and pollution control board certificate, which are marked at Ex.P12 to Ex.P17.
On perusal of the same it is clear that the policy is in existence as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
36. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,96,163/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized/scheduled bank for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
